trial_name: Chlorophyllin for Toxic Effect Prevention During Total Neoadjuvant Therapy in Rectal Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial
setting: Supportive care during total neoadjuvant therapy
primary_title: Chlorophyllin for Toxic Effect Prevention During Total Neoadjuvant Therapy in Rectal Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial
primary_endpoint: CTCAE v5.0 grade ≥2 combined acute GI, hematologic or GU toxicity through 3 months after TNT
primary_results: 24/37 (65%) versus 34/36 (94%); absolute risk reduction 29.6 percentage points (90% CI 15.2–43.9); RR 0.69 (90% CI 0.56–0.86), p=0.003; NNT 4.
secondary_results: Grade ≥3 combined acute toxicity 10/37 (27%) versus 19/36 (53%); absolute risk reduction 25.8 percentage points (90% CI 7.5–44.0); RR 0.51 (90% CI 0.30–0.86), p=0.03; NNT 4.
why_today: Published 25 November 2026; genuinely new to the Atlas and within the preceding month. No roster, canonical page, archive or prior Trial-of-the-Day match was found.
summary: A phase II double-blind trial found lower acute grade ≥2 and grade ≥3 toxicity with oral sodium copper chlorophyllin during TNT for locally advanced rectal cancer.
source_note: Primary JAMA Oncology abstract used; full article not mined. No QoL or long-term oncologic outcomes were reported in the accessible abstract.
